display.purpose: Header anchor only — total energy produced, civilisation level. The one display-scale text.

body.purpose: Row names, figures, drawer copy, modal copy. Barlow Condensed carries all of it.

label.purpose: Time-codes, column headers, section labels; uppercase, wide tracking, ink-faint.

shadows.name: steel-dome
shadows.purpose: The brushed-steel frame reads as a slightly domed panel. Header, terminal bar, modal head.

shadows.name: machined-lip
shadows.purpose: The LANCER master control — the only element lifted off the board.

shadows.name: flap-hinge
shadows.purpose: The 2px shadow across the middle of a flap character cell (a ::after bar, not a box-shadow).

shadows.name: floating-chrome
shadows.purpose: Toasts and other transient chrome above the board.

shadows.name: lamp-glow
shadows.purpose: A trend lamp's own-colour glow — the only glow on the surface.

motion.name: flap-flip
motion.purpose: The split-flap cascade. perspective(160px) rotateX fold at the hinge. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion (instant swap).

motion.name: drawer-slide
motion.purpose: The service-row detail drawer opening in place.

breakpoints.name: board
breakpoints.purpose: Terminal selector moves from fixed-bottom to sticky-top; readouts go inline in the header; service rows cap tighter and gain the dotted leader.

breakpoints.name: board-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Service list max-width widens from ~46rem to ~52rem.

components.name: Service Row
components.description: The board's atom — one buyable line. Whole row is the buy action; the chevron opens a detail drawer in place. State (afford / cant / locked / done) is carried by data-state and shows mostly in the fare colour.

components.name: Split-Flap Figure
components.description: A row of flap character cells. On value change only the changed cells flip, cascading left to right. The mid-cell hinge shadow is a ::after bar. Every resource figure and the LANCER +N use this.
components.html: 148 260

components.name: LANCER control
components.description: The master input. Full-width machined-lip bar; tap = one click, hold = auto-cadence with an amber inner ring; :active presses in.

components.name: Terminal Button
components.description: One of five in the sticky terminal selector. Pictogram over uppercase label. Active = matte board-black inset with an amber leading-edge bar.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The buy / build / research / ascend action inside a row drawer or the ascension panel.

components.name: Announcement Strip
components.description: Station-PA banner above the terminal bar. Level colour rides the pictogram and a left-edge gradient wash — never a coloured border-left.

narrative.overview: The game is a public departures board for a spacefaring civilisation. Not a dashboard, not a HUD over a starfield, not the idle-game scroll of same-size buy-cards — a single physical board of matte flap faces set in a brushed-steel frame. Every quantity the player owns is a ruled row on that board; every number that moves flips character by character, a cascade running left to right. The surface commits to one material world: a warm matte near-black ground, painted-white letters with a hairline of paint shadow, a real brushed-aluminium frame (a generated noise texture, never a CSS bevel). Colour is rationed to three signal roles — amber when you can't afford something, green when you can, dim signal-red for locked or terminated — plus a cool blue focus ring. Density is high and legible: ruled rows, fixed columns, tabular figures, one condensed grotesque (Barlow Condensed, from highway signage) for every word. The one concession to scale is the header, which leads with the two numbers that tell you how far you've come, the way a concourse board leads with its clock.
keyCharacteristics: One ruled board; no cards, ever.
Any changing number changes by flap cascade, digit by digit.
One typeface (Barlow Condensed) for every word.
Warm matte near-black ground; painted-white letters; brushed-steel frame.
Colour is signal only: amber = can't afford, green = affordable, red = locked.
Real generated textures (brushed metal, paint grain), never faked bevels.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: Cost colour IS the affordability state. Amber means you cannot pay; green means you can. Never show a cost in neutral ink — the player reads the board by colour first.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: The three accents (amber, green, red) are points and 1px marks, never fills over a region. If an accent owns more than a lamp, a short word, or a hairline, it has stopped being a signal.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed carries every word on the surface. There is no second family — no serif, no mono, no system-sans body face. A departures board is lettered once.

rules.name: The Painted-Letter Rule
rules.body: Display text on the matte ground carries text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.45) — the shadow of paint sitting proud of the metal. Body copy does not get it.

rules.name: The Real-Material Rule
rules.body: Metal and paint are generated textures (SVG feTurbulence tiles blended over a gradient). CSS bevels, embossing, and zero-blur block shadows imitating a material the page never renders are banned — the machined lip on .launch is the single sanctioned dimensional treatment.

dos: Do put every quantity on a ruled row of the one board. New content is a new row or a new section of rows, never a card or a panel.
Do route any on-screen number that changes through the split-flap display so it flaps digit by digit; honour prefers-reduced-motion with an instant swap.
Do set every word in Barlow Condensed, uppercase for names and labels, with tabular numerals.
Do colour costs by affordability — Active Green when payable, Lamp Amber when not — and never in neutral ink.
Do build metal and paint as generated textures; keep the machined lip on .launch as the only dimensional element.
Do give the header the two lead numbers (total produced, civilisation level) at display scale as the page's anchor.
Do open detail in place with the row drawer's mechanical slide.
donts: Don't introduce cards, boxed panels, rounded containers, or elevation on rows. Nested cards especially.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons — only the authored 24-grid pictogram set.
Don't add a second typeface, gradient text, glass/blur decoration, or a coloured border-left above 1px on any strip or alert.
Don't use a zero-blur block shadow (box-shadow: 0 Ypx 0 …) — the neobrutalist ledge is not this world.
Don't put a starfield, nebula, or neon-HUD chrome behind the board.
Don't let an accent (amber / green / red) own a region; it is a lamp, a word, or a hairline.
Don't flatten or remove the flap cascade to "simplify" — it is the thesis.
